title: prefetch
nav_title: prefetch
description: Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function.
related:
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
    - app/api-reference/functions/connection
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
---

Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.

Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

---
title: prefetch
nav_title: prefetch
description: Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function.
related:
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
    - app/api-reference/functions/connection
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
---

Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.

Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

---
title: Optimizing prefetching
description: Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage.
nav_title: Optimizing prefetching
related:
  title: Learn more
  description: Learn more about the APIs and concepts used in this guide.
  links:
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching

    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
---

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):

1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.

title: instant
description: Configure instant navigation validation for a route segment.

---

The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.

Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.

When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.

---
title: instant
description: Configure instant navigation validation for a route segment.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic
    - app/getting-started/caching
    - app/getting-started/revalidating
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
---

The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.

Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.

When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.

Before [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), route segment configs such as [`dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic), `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, and `dynamic = 'error'` selected a rendering mode for an entire route. Cache Components lets one route combine prerendered UI, cached content, and request-specific content rendered at request time.

This flexibility is useful for routes that need personalization. Use [`ensureStatic`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic) when some or all of a route must avoid request-time server rendering for predictable performance and compute costs.

## Decide what should stay static

Static output does not depend on request-specific data. Next.js can generate it before a request and reuse it across requests.

---
title: Keeping pages static
description: Keep selected route output static as your app changes.
nav_title: Keeping pages static
related:
  title: API reference
  description: Require static output across a route or defer work within one subtree.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic
    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
---

Before [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), route segment configs such as [`dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic), `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, and `dynamic = 'error'` selected a rendering mode for an entire route. Cache Components lets one route combine prerendered UI, cached content, and request-specific content rendered at request time.

This flexibility is useful for routes that need personalization. Use [`ensureStatic`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic) when some or all of a route must avoid request-time server rendering for predictable performance and compute costs.

## Decide what should stay static

Static output does not depend on request-specific data. Next.js can generate it before a request and reuse it across requests.

00038| 
00039| ## Reference
00040| 
00041| The export accepts `'auto'`, `'shell'`, `'prefetch'`, `'navigation'`, or `false`. The default is `'auto'`, which is equivalent to omitting the export.
00042| 
00043| `ensureStatic` controls which server-rendered output must be static. With Partial Prefetching, that output can be the App Shell, an optional per-link prefetch, or the complete route rendered during navigation. These outputs are called [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages). Each stricter level also includes the earlier stages.
00044| 
00045| | Value              | Output that must be static       |
00046| | ------------------ | -------------------------------- |
00047| | `'auto'` (default) | No additional static requirement |
00048| | `'shell'`          | App Shell                        |
00049| | `'prefetch'`       | App Shell and per-link prefetch  |
00050| | `'navigation'`     | Complete server-rendered route   |
00051| 
00052| `false` does not select a static level. It preserves normal rendering behavior and prevents another segment from applying `'shell'`, `'prefetch'`, or `'navigation'` to the route. See [`false`](#false).
00053| 
00054| ### `'shell'`
00055| 
00056| Requires the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) loaded by a default `<Link>` to be static. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) there is no App Shell, so the value has no effect and Next.js logs a warning.
00057| 
00058| The shell can include static or cached content and `<Suspense>` fallbacks. Request-specific content behind `<Suspense>` can render during a later per-link prefetch with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or during navigation.
00059| 
00060| For an individual subtree, [`await prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) provides similar behavior by deferring code below the call to a per-link prefetch or navigation. Setting `'shell'` enforces that stage boundary across the route without adding `await prefetch()` to each request-specific subtree. See [Defer work to a later stage](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#defer-work-to-a-later-stage) for the per-subtree controls.
00061| 
00062| > **Good to know**: `'shell'` does not require per-link prefetches to be static. If the route reads `cookies()`, `headers()`, or URL data before [`await navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation), each visible [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) can still trigger a server render. Use [`'prefetch'`](#prefetch) when per-link prefetches must also come from static output.
00063| 
00064| ### `'prefetch'`
00065| 
00066| Requires both the App Shell and per-link prefetches to be static. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), the value adds no requirement and links keep their normal full-prefetch behavior. A full prefetch can include request-specific data and is not guaranteed to be static.
00067| 
00068| A per-link prefetch from [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) can load static or cached [URL-specific content](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#resolve-url-data-at-prefetch-time) before the user follows the link. Request-specific content behind `<Suspense>` renders when the navigation completes the route.
00069| 
00070| The [static HTML shell](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) can also include this static or cached per-link content. Unlike a per-link prefetch, it cannot include request-specific data because the HTML shell is prerendered.
00071| 
00072| For an individual subtree, [`await navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) provides similar behavior by deferring code below the call until navigation. Setting `'prefetch'` enforces that stage boundary across the route without adding `await navigation()` to each request-specific subtree. See [Keep the prefetch static](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#keep-the-prefetch-static) for shaping one route this way.
00073| 
00074| ### `'navigation'`
00075| 
00076| Requires the complete server-rendered route to be produced during prerendering, so initial loads and client navigations use static output. This value works with Cache Components alone and does not require Partial Prefetching.
00077| 
00078| To require static server output for the entire app, set `'navigation'` on the root layout. See [Combining levels across layouts and pages](#combining-levels-across-layouts-and-pages) for how levels apply across a route.
00079| 
00080| #### Validation
00081| 
00082| With `'shell'` and `'prefetch'`, request-specific work inside `<Suspense>` can move to a later navigation stage. These values do not add build validation. When [Instant Navigation validation](/docs/messages/instant-navigation-validation) is enabled, it can report request-specific work outside `<Suspense>` because it blocks the navigation.
00083| 
00084| `'navigation'` is the final server-rendering stage, so no later stage remains. Next.js validates its complete static-output requirement during both `next dev` and `next build`. In development, errors include source-mapped stack traces that update as you edit. Build output is more abbreviated, so you may need to run [`next build --debug-prerender`](/docs/app/guides/building#debug-prerender-errors) for detailed stack traces and code frames. See [Ensuring instant navigations](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for the development workflow.
00085| 
00086| With `ensureStatic = 'navigation'`, the following server content fails validation, even when it is wrapped in `<Suspense>` or the segment sets [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#disabling-instant):
00087| 
00088| - [Uncached data](/docs/messages/static-route-dynamic), including a `fetch` or database call without [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache), and [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection).
00089| - [Runtime data](/docs/messages/static-route-runtime), such as `cookies()`, `headers()`, and server-side `searchParams`.
00090| - A `use cache` scope whose [`expire`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#expire) is under five minutes, [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) is under 30 seconds, or [`revalidate`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#revalidate) is `0`. A `stale` time between 30 seconds and five minutes is allowed.
00091| - A promise for request-dependent server data passed to a Client Component, whether or not the component reads it.
00092| 
00093| These constraints also apply to [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) and [`generateViewport`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-viewport).
00094| 
00095| Data cached with `use cache` can be prerendered. [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) and [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) are also allowed because a static prerender continues through their stage boundaries.
00096| 
00097| #### Dynamic route parameters
00098| 
00099| With `'navigation'`, a dynamic route must export [`generateStaticParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) and return at least one complete parameter set. Each result must include every dynamic parameter in the route, even if the parameter is unused or only read in a Client Component.
00100| 
00101| Values returned by `generateStaticParams()` are available during prerendering. When a request uses a value that was not prerendered at build time, Next.js waits for the static result to be generated before serving it.
00102| 
00103| With `'shell'` or `'prefetch'`, a value that was not prerendered serves the route's fallback shell instead, with `<Suspense>` fallbacks in place of its content, while Next.js generates the page in the background. See [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components#at-runtime).
00104| 
00105| The build fails when `generateStaticParams()` is missing or returns an incomplete parameter set. See the [`generateStaticParams` error guide](/docs/messages/generate-static-params#with-ensurestatic).
00106| 
00107| #### Client Components
00108| 
00109| Client Components can load request-specific content in the browser. Inside `<Suspense>`, `use(browser())` and [`use(io())`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/io) are allowed. The prerender includes the fallback for the deferred content. See [Rendering components only in the browser](/docs/app/guides/single-page-applications#rendering-components-only-in-the-browser).
00110| 
00111| Client hooks such as [`useParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-params) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) are also allowed. Dynamic routes still require `generateStaticParams()`. Passing a request-dependent promise from a Server Component still requires server work and produces an error.
00112| 
00113| ### `false`
00114| 
00115| With Partial Prefetching, `false` keeps the route's normal rendering behavior and fails the build if another segment sets `'shell'`, `'prefetch'`, or `'navigation'`. Use it to signal that a segment is not meant to be statically optimized.
00116| 
00117| ## How `ensureStatic` differs from `instant`
00118| 
00119| `ensureStatic` requires selected server-rendered output to avoid request-time work. Use it when the App Shell, a per-link prefetch, or the complete route must be static.
00120| 
00121| [`instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) validates whether a navigation can update the UI immediately. Cached or prerendered UI can satisfy this requirement while request-specific content streams later behind `<Suspense>`.
00122| 
00123| Setting `instant = false` disables Instant Navigation validation for the route. The `'shell'` and `'prefetch'` values still make the client request the corresponding static output, but neither value adds separate build validation. A static prefetch can still include a parent layout, metadata, and Client Component preload hints even when the page UI renders only after the user follows the link. The `'navigation'` value uses separate complete static-output validation, which `instant = false` does not relax.
00124| 
00125| ## Combining levels across layouts and pages
00126| 
00127| A level set on the root layout applies to every route in the app. A level set on another layout applies to every route that renders it, including its nested layouts, pages, and [parallel routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes). Within a route, the level covers every segment, including the layouts above the one that sets it.
00128| 
00129| Leaving the export unset or setting it to `'auto'` is compatible with any level and preserves another segment's setting. A descendant can set a stricter static level, but not a weaker one:
00130| 
00131| ```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx"
00132| export const ensureStatic = 'prefetch'
00133| ```
00134| 
00135| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx"
00136| export const ensureStatic = 'navigation' // allowed, stricter than 'prefetch'
00137| ```
00138| 
00139| A weaker level on a child segment fails the build:
00140| 
00141| ```text filename="Terminal"
00142| A child segment cannot override a parent segment with a less-constrained `ensureStatic`.
00143| ```
00144| 
00145| Mixing `false` with `'shell'`, `'prefetch'`, or `'navigation'` in a parent and child fails with:
00146| 
00147| ```text filename="Terminal"
00148| A child segment cannot override a parent segment with an incompatible `ensureStatic`.
00149| ```
00150| 
00151| Parallel routes rendered together must set the same value, leave the export unset, or use `'auto'`. Conflicting values fail with:
00152| 
00153| ```text filename="Terminal"
00154| Parallel slots cannot have incompatible `ensureStatic`.
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| ## TypeScript
00158| 
00159| ```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx"
00160| type EnsureStatic = 'auto' | 'shell' | 'prefetch' | 'navigation' | false
00161| 
00162| export const ensureStatic: EnsureStatic = 'navigation'
00163| ```
00164|

00166| 
00167| | Version   | Changes                    |
00168| | --------- | -------------------------- |
00169| | `v16.4.0` | `ensureStatic` introduced. |

00041| The export accepts `'auto'`, `'shell'`, `'prefetch'`, `'navigation'`, or `false`. The default is `'auto'`, which is equivalent to omitting the export.

00043| `ensureStatic` controls which server-rendered output must be static. These outputs are called [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages). Each stricter level also includes the earlier stages.
00044| 
00045| | Value              | Output that must be static       |
00046| | ------------------ | -------------------------------- |
00047| | `'auto'` (default) | No additional static requirement |
00048| | `'shell'`          | App Shell                        |
00049| | `'prefetch'`       | App Shell and per-link prefetch  |
00050| | `'navigation'`     | Complete server-rendered route   |
00051| 
00052| `false` does not select a static level. It preserves normal rendering behavior and prevents another segment from applying `'shell'`, `'prefetch'`, or `'navigation'` to the route. See [`false`](#false).

00054| ### `'shell'`
00055| 
00056| Requires the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) loaded by a default `<Link>` to be static. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) there is no App Shell, so the value has no effect and Next.js logs a warning.
00057| 
00058| The shell can include static or cached content and `<Suspense>` fallbacks. Request-specific content behind `<Suspense>` can render during a later per-link prefetch with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or during navigation.
00059| 
00060| For an individual subtree, [`await prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) provides similar behavior by deferring code below the call to a per-link prefetch or navigation. Setting `'shell'` enforces that stage boundary across the route without adding `await prefetch()` to each request-specific subtree. See [Defer work to a later stage](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#defer-work-to-a-later-stage) for the per-subtree controls.
00061| 
00062| > **Good to know**: `'shell'` does not require per-link prefetches to be static. Use [`'prefetch'`](#prefetch) when per-link prefetches must also come from static output.
00063| 
00064| ### `'prefetch'`
00065| 
00066| Requires both the App Shell and per-link prefetches to be static. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), the value adds no requirement and links keep their normal full-prefetch behavior. A full prefetch can include request-specific data and is not guaranteed to be static.
00067| 
00068| A per-link prefetch from [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch) can load static or cached [URL-specific content](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#resolve-url-data-at-prefetch-time) before the user follows the link. 00081| 
00082| With `'shell'` and `'prefetch'`, request-specific work inside `<Suspense>` can move to a later navigation stage. These values do not add build validation. 00088| - [Uncached data](/docs/messages/static-route-dynamic), including a `fetch` or database call without [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache), and [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection).

00090| - A `use cache` scope whose [`expire`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#expire) is under five minutes, [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) is under 30 seconds, or [`revalidate`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#revalidate) is `0`. 00094| 
00095| Data cached with `use cache` can be prerendered. [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) and [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) are also allowed because a static prerender continues through their stage boundaries.

00098| 
00099| With `'navigation'`, a dynamic route must export [`generateStaticParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) and return at least one complete parameter set. 00101| Values returned by `generateStaticParams()` are available during prerendering. When a request uses a value that was not prerendered at build time, Next.js waits for the static result to be generated before serving it.
00102| 
00103| With `'shell'` or `'prefetch'`, a value that was not prerendered serves the route's fallback shell instead, with `<Suspense>` fallbacks in place of its content, while Next.js generates the page in the background. 00104| 
00105| The build fails when `generateStaticParams()` is missing or returns an incomplete parameter set. See the [`generateStaticParams` error guide](/docs/messages/generate-static-params#with-ensurestatic).
00106| 
00107| #### Client Components
00108| 
00109| Client Components can load request-specific content in the browser. Inside `<Suspense>`, `use(browser())` and [`use(io())`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/io) are allowed. 00110| 
00111| Client hooks such as [`useParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-params) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) are also allowed. 00112|

00114| 
00115| With Partial Prefetching, `false` keeps the route's normal rendering behavior and fails the build if another segment sets `'shell'`, `'prefetch'`, or `'navigation'`. Use it to signal that a segment is not meant to be statically optimized.
00116| 
00117| ## How `ensureStatic` differs from `instant`
00118| 
00119| `ensureStatic` requires selected server-rendered output to avoid request-time work. Use it when the App Shell, a per-link prefetch, or the complete route must be static.
00120| 
00121| [`instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) validates whether a navigation can update the UI immediately. Cached or prerendered UI can satisfy this requirement while request-specific content streams later behind `<Suspense>`.
00122| 
00123| Setting `instant = false` disables Instant Navigation validation for the route. 00124| 
00125| ## Combining levels across layouts and pages
00126| 
00127| A level set on the root layout applies to every route in the app. A level set on another layout applies to every route that renders it, including its nested layouts, pages, and [parallel routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes). 00129| Leaving the export unset or setting it to `'auto'` is compatible with any level and preserves another segment's setting. A descendant can set a stricter static level, but not a weaker one:
00130| 
00131| ```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx"

00133| ```
00134| 
00135| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx"
00136| export const ensureStatic = 'navigation' // allowed, stricter than 'prefetch'
00137| ```
00138| 
00139| A weaker level on a child segment fails the build:
00140| 
00141| ```text filename="Terminal"
00142| A child segment cannot override a parent segment with a less-constrained `ensureStatic`.
00143| ```
00144| 
00145| Mixing `false` with `'shell'`, `'prefetch'`, or `'navigation'` in a parent and child fails with:
00146| 
00147| ```text filename="Terminal"
00148| A child segment cannot override a parent segment with an incompatible `ensureStatic`.
00149| ```
00150| 
00151| Parallel routes rendered together must set the same value, leave the export unset, or use `'auto'`. Conflicting values fail with:
00152| 
00153| ```text filename="Terminal"
00154| Parallel slots cannot have incompatible `ensureStatic`.
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| ## TypeScript
00158| 
00159| ```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx"
00160| type EnsureStatic = 'auto' | 'shell' | 'prefetch' | 'navigation' | false
00161| 
00162| export const ensureStatic: EnsureStatic = 'navigation'
00163| ```
00164| 
00165| ## Version History
00166| 
00167| | Version   | Changes                    |
00168| | --------- | -------------------------- |
00169| | `v16.4.0` | `ensureStatic` introduced. |
00170|

title: ensureStatic
description: Require selected route output to remain static instead of rendering per request with the ensureStatic route segment config.

The `ensureStatic` route segment config requires selected route output to be static instead of rendered per request. title: navigation
nav_title: navigation
description: Defer runtime work until the user navigates with the navigation function.
related:
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
    - app/api-reference/functions/connection
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
---

Calling `await navigation()` keeps runtime work below it out of the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and per-link prefetches. The work runs when the user navigates, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the prefetched output.

Use `navigation()` for reusable content that is expensive to generate and should wait until navigation. Static prerenders still include the content in their output, so it can appear in a static prefetch.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), and throws without it. It is meant for routes using [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), which you can enable globally or one route at a time by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

metadata.preview:
---
title: navigation
nav_title: navigation
description: Defer runtime work until the user navigates with the navigation function.
related:
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
    - app/api-reference/functions/connection
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
---

Calling `await navigation()` keeps runtime work below it out of the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and per-link prefetches. The work runs when the user navigates, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the prefetched output.

Use `navigation()` for reusable content that is expensive to generate and should wait until navigation. Static prerenders still include the content in their output, so it can appear in a static prefetch.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), and throws without it. It is meant for routes using [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), which you can enable globally or one route at a time by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

00014| 
00015| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00016| 
00017| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00018| 
00019| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022|

00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
00088| 
00089| ### Verify prefetched UI with tests
00090| 
00091| To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
00092| 
00093| ```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
00094| import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
00095| import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
00096| 
00097| test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
00098|   await page.goto('/products')
00099| 
00100|   await instant(page, async () => {
00101|     const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
00102|     await expect(link).toBeVisible()
00103|     await link.click()
00104|     await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
00105| 
00106|     await expect(
00107|       page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
00108|     ).toBeVisible()
00109|     await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
00110|   })
00111| })
00112| ```
00113| 
00114| Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. If it fails, the selected UI is no longer prefetched. Cache the reusable data or subtree that should stay available, then keep the passing test as regression coverage.
00115|

00267| ### URL data
00268| 
00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00270| 
00271| ### Real-time content
00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00274| 
00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00281| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

00283| ## Adopting incrementally
00284| 
00285| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00286| 
00287| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:

00474| ## Prefetching URL data
00475| 
00476| Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) resolves it ahead of the click for links with `prefetch={true}`, at the cost of a server invocation per prefetchable link. To make the content resolvable at prefetch time, cache it behind the read with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). For a search page that reads `searchParams`:

title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
description: Learn how to enable Partial Prefetching and what changes for `<Link>`.
related:
  title: Next Steps

  links:

---

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00026| 
00027| Install the skill:
00028| 
00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Then give the agent this prompt:
00034| 
00035| ```prompt
00036| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. 00088| 
00089| ### Verify prefetched UI with tests
00090| 
00091| To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. 00097| test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
00098|   await page.goto('/products')

00100|   await instant(page, async () => {

00102|     await expect(link).toBeVisible()
00103|     await link.click()
00104|     await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')

00176| 
00177| Content behind [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) varies per session, not per link, and [session data resolves in the App Shell](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#include-session-data-in-the-shell), so cached session content still gets included. 00179| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher

00182| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

00267| ### URL data
00268| 
00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00270| 
00271| ### Real-time content
00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00274| 
00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00281| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
00282| 
00283| ## Adopting incrementally
00284| 
00285| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00286| 
00287| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:

00289| <FixCardGrid>
00290|   <FixCard
00291|     group="upgrade"
00292|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00293|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"

00305|       { text: '  Dashboard' },

00307|     ]}

00312| 
00313| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00314| 
00315|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00316|    // Before
00317|    export default function Page() {
00318|      return <Dashboard />
00319|    }
00320|    ```
00321| 
00322|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00323|    // Before
00324|    export default function Page() {
00325|      return <Dashboard />
00326|    }
00327|    ```
00328| 
00329|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00330|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00331|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00332| 
00333|    export default function Page() {
00334|      return <Dashboard />
00335|    }
00336|    ```
00337| 
00338|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00339|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00340|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00341| 
00342|    export default function Page() {
00343|      return <Dashboard />
00344|    }
00345|    ```
00346| 
00347|    > **Good to know**: If the page or layout already calls [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch), import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, so it doesn't collide with the `prefetch` export.
00348| 
00349| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00350| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).
00351| 
00352| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:
00353| 
00354| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00355| npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app
00356| ```
00357| 
00358| > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count.
00359| 
00360| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.

00362| ## Move URL data behind Suspense

00364| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. 00013| ---
00014| 
00015| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00016| 
00017| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00018| 
00019| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00020| 
00021| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00022| 
00023| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00024| 
00025| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00026| 
00027| Install the skill:
00028| 
00029| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Then give the agent this prompt:
00034| 
00035| ```prompt
00036| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ## Or adopt by hand
00040| 
00041| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00042| 
00043| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00044| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00045| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00046| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00047| 
00048| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00049| 
00050| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00053| 
00054| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00055| 
00056| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00057| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00058| 
00059| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00060|   cacheComponents: true,
00061|   partialPrefetching: true,
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default nextConfig
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00068| 
00069| > **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00070| 
00071| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00072| 
00073| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00074| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00075| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00076| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00078| 
00079| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00080| 
00081| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00082| 
00083| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00084| 
00085| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00086| 
00087| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.

00096| 
00097| test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
00098|   await page.goto('/products')
00099| 
00100|   await instant(page, async () => {

00102|     await expect(link).toBeVisible()

00271| ### Real-time content
00272|

00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00277| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00278| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00279| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |

00282| 
00283| ## Adopting incrementally
00284| 
00285| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00286| 
00287| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:
00288| 
00289| <FixCardGrid>
00290|   <FixCard
00291|     group="upgrade"
00292|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00293|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"
00294|     snippets={[
00295|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00296|       { text: "export const prefetch = 'partial'", highlight: true },
00297|     ]}
00298|   />
00299|   <FixCard
00300|     group="disable"
00301|     title="Use the default prefetch"
00302|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#use-the-default-prefetch"
00303|     snippets={[
00304|       { text: '<Link href="/dashboard">', highlight: true },
00305|       { text: '  Dashboard' },
00306|       { text: '</Link>' },
00307|     ]}
00308|   />
00309| </FixCardGrid>
00310| 
00311| Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs.
00312| 
00313| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00314| 
00315|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00316|    // Before
00317|    export default function Page() {
00318|      return <Dashboard />
00319|    }
00320|    ```
00321| 
00322|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00323|    // Before
00324|    export default function Page() {
00325|      return <Dashboard />
00326|    }
00327|    ```
00328| 
00329|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00330|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00331|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00332| 
00333|    export default function Page() {
00334|      return <Dashboard />
00335|    }
00336|    ```
00337| 
00338|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00339|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00340|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00341| 
00342|    export default function Page() {
00343|      return <Dashboard />
00344|    }
00345|    ```
00346| 
00347|    > **Good to know**: If the page or layout already calls [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch), import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, so it doesn't collide with the `prefetch` export.
00348| 
00349| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00350| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).
00351| 
00352| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:
00353| 
00354| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00355| npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app
00356| ```
00357| 
00358| > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count.
00359| 
00360| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.
00361| 
00362| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00363| 
00364| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. The App Shell is shared across every link to a route, so it can't contain data that belongs to a single URL. Reading [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) or [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) outside a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary ties the shell to the link's URL and surfaces the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight, naming the route and pointing at its fixes:
00365| 
00366| <FixCardGrid>
00367|   <FixCard
00368|     group="stream"
00369|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
00370|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"
00371|     snippets={[
00372|       { text: '<Suspense fallback={…}>', highlight: true },
00373|       { text: '  <Details params={params} />' },
00374|       { text: '</Suspense>', highlight: true },
00375|     ]}
00376|   />
00377|   <FixCard
00378|     group="block"
00379|     title="Allow blocking route"
00380|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#allow-blocking-route"
00381|     snippets={[
00382|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00383|       { text: 'export const instant = false', highlight: true },
00384|     ]}
00385|   />
00386| </FixCardGrid>
00387| 
00388| The insight never blocks the build, so this pass can happen any time after the flag is on. Load every route in `next dev` to check for it.
00389| 
00390| The fix is to keep the URL-independent parts of the route outside the boundary and move the `params` or `searchParams` read into a child wrapped in `<Suspense>`:
00391| 
00392| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00393| // Before - awaiting params at the top ties the App Shell to one URL
00394| export default async function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00395|   const { slug } = await params
00396|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00397|   return (
00398|     <ProductLayout>
00399|       <Details product={product} />
00400|     </ProductLayout>
00401|   )
00402| }
00403| ```
00404| 
00405| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00406| // Before - awaiting params at the top ties the App Shell to one URL
00407| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00408|   const { slug } = await params
00409|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00410|   return (
00411|     <ProductLayout>
00412|       <Details product={product} />
00413|     </ProductLayout>
00414|   )
00415| }
00416| ```
00417| 
00418| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00419| // After - pass the promise down without awaiting it
00420| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00421| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00422| 
00423| export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00424|   return (
00425|     <ProductLayout>
00426|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00427|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00428|       </Suspense>
00429|     </ProductLayout>
00430|   )
00431| }
00432| ```
00433| 
00434| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00435| // After - pass the promise down without awaiting it
00436| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00437| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00438| 
00439| export default function Page({ params }) {
00440|   return (
00441|     <ProductLayout>
00442|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00443|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00444|       </Suspense>
00445|     </ProductLayout>
00446|   )
00447| }
00448| ```
00449| 
00450| The child awaits the promise inside the boundary:
00451| 
00452| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/product-details.tsx" switcher
00453| export async function ProductDetails({
00454|   params,
00455| }: Pick<PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>, 'params'>) {
00456|   const { slug } = await params
00457|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00458|   return <Details product={product} />
00459| }
00460| ```
00461| 
00462| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/product-details.js" switcher
00463| export async function ProductDetails({ params }) {
00464|   const { slug } = await params
00465|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00466|   return <Details product={product} />
00467| }
00468| ```
00469| 
00470| Everything outside the boundary stays in the shared App Shell, and only the URL-specific region renders per navigation. Load or navigate to the route again to confirm the insight is gone and the page still paints meaningful UI.
00471| 
00472| > **Good to know**: A `params` or `searchParams` read inside [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) surfaces as [URL data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) instead.
00473| 
00474| ## Prefetching URL data
00475| 
00476| Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) resolves it ahead of the click for links with `prefetch={true}`, at the cost of a server invocation per prefetchable link. To make the content resolvable at prefetch time, cache it behind the read with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). For a search page that reads `searchParams`:
00477| 
00478| ```tsx filename="app/search/page.tsx" switcher
00479| // Before - the results stream in after navigation
00480| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00481| 
00482| async function getResults(query: string) {
00483|   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/search?q=${query}`)
00484|   return res.json()
00485| }
00486| 
00487| async function Results({
00488|   searchParams,
00489| }: Pick<PageProps<'/search'>, 'searchParams'>) {
00490|   const { q } = await searchParams
00491|   return <ResultList results={await getResults(q)} />
00492| }
00493| 
00494| export default function Page({ searchParams }: PageProps<'/search'>) {
00495|   return (
00496|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00497|       <Results searchParams={searchParams} />
00498|     </Suspense>
00499|   )
00500| }
00501| ```
00502| 
00503| ```jsx filename="app/search/page.js" switcher
00504| // Before - the results stream in after navigation
00505| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00506| 
00507| async function getResults(query) {
00508|   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/search?q=${query}`)
00509|   return res.json()
00510| }
00511| 
00512| async function Results({ searchParams }) {
00513|   const { q } = await searchParams
00514|   return <ResultList results={await getResults(q)} />
00515| }
00516| 
00517| export default function Page({ searchParams }) {
00518|   return (
00519|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00520|       <Results searchParams={searchParams} />
00521|     </Suspense>
00522|   )
00523| }
00524| ```
00525| 
00526| ```tsx filename="app/search/page.tsx" switcher
00527| // After - the results are cached and prefetched behind the resolved searchParams
00528| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00529| 
00530| async function getResults(query: string) {
00531|   'use cache'
00532|   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/search?q=${query}`)
00533|   return res.json()
00534| }
00535| 
00536| async function Results({
00537|   searchParams,
00538| }: Pick<PageProps<'/search'>, 'searchParams'>) {
00539|   const { q } = await searchParams
00540|   return <ResultList results={await getResults(q)} />
00541| }
00542| 
00543| export default function Page({ searchParams }: PageProps<'/search'>) {
00544|   return (
00545|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00546|       <Results searchParams={searchParams} />
00547|     </Suspense>
00548|   )
00549| }
00550| ```
00551| 
00552| ```jsx filename="app/search/page.js" switcher
00553| // After - the results are cached and prefetched behind the resolved searchParams
00554| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00555| 
00556| async function getResults(query) {
00557|   'use cache'
00558|   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/search?q=${query}`)
00559|   return res.json()
00560| }
00561| 
00562| async function Results({ searchParams }) {
00563|   const { q } = await searchParams
00564|   return <ResultList results={await getResults(q)} />
00565| }
00566| 
00567| export default function Page({ searchParams }) {
00568|   return (
00569|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00570|       <Results searchParams={searchParams} />
00571|     </Suspense>
00572|   )
00573| }
